key_insight: ACE and its graph generalization GRACE provide a common representation of many interatomic potentials, revealing efficiency choices behind apparently different architectures.
engineering_relevance: Selecting model complexity along an accuracy–speed Pareto front can reduce atomistic simulation costs while preserving the accuracy required for materials discovery.
method: Represent classical and machine learning potentials using canonical products of single-particle functions.
Compare nonlinear parameterizations, layer coupling and optimization within the shared ACE/GRACE framework.
Analyze linear cost scaling with system size and, at fixed tensor-decomposition rank, model complexity.
evidence_signal: The review reports that three- to five-layer models approach deeper-model accuracy on Matbench Discovery, while Pareto-guided truncation of one basis spans more than two orders of magnitude in cost.
watch_item: Training data ultimately determine potential quality, so efficiency gains must be assessed at the accuracy required for the target application.
